_qms_instructions.purpose: Single Source of Truth for NHS Ayrshire & Arran Clinical Biochemistry Test Directory (LFB-CLI-003-WEB).
_qms_instructions.how_to_update: 1. Update 'qmsMetadata' (handbookVersion, effectiveDate, nextReviewDate, authorisedBy). 2. Edit/add entries in 'tests'. 3. Upload updated tests.json to GitHub Pages or AthenA.

field_reference.name: Primary assay or profile display name
field_reference.trakCode: OrderComms / TrakCare test code (N/O = Not Orderable electronically)
field_reference.tubeType: Required Monovette/container (Draw order: 1. White 7.5mL, 2. Green Citrate, 3. Orange 5.5mL Li-Hep, 4. Yellow 2.7mL Fluoride, 5. Red 2.7mL K-EDTA)
field_reference.tubeColor: Visual badge key: orange, white, red, yellow, universal, urine24, faeces-blue, qfit, bloodspot, specialist
field_reference.sampleType: Blood, Urine, CSF, Fluid, Faeces, Sweat, or Stone
field_reference.referenceRange: Adult reference range and clinical interpretation notes
field_reference.paediatricRanges: Age-adjusted reference ranges from Appendix 2 (if applicable)
field_reference.addOnStability: Maximum add-on window (72h standard unless listed in stability table)
field_reference.telephoneAlert: Appendix 1 critical result telephone thresholds (if applicable)
field_reference.specialPrecautions: Boolean: true if time-critical arrival, light protection, warm flask, no pneumatic tube, or Duty Biochemist pre-arrangement required
field_reference.collectionNotes: Specific collection, timing, storage, and transport instructions
field_reference.synonyms: Search keywords, clinical syndromes, and abbreviations

qmsMetadata.sourceHandbookTitle: NHS Ayrshire & Arran Clinical Biochemistry Laboratory Handbook
qmsMetadata.author: Terri Collins
qmsMetadata.authorisedBy: Dr Scott Blackwell / Mrs Janet Hogg

tests.name: Urea, Creatinine & Electrolytes Profile (U&Es)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: Na: 133-146 mmol/L | K: 3.5-5.3 mmol/L | Cl: 95-108 mmol/L | Urea: 2.5-7.8 mmol/L | Creatinine: M 50-120, F 50-100 µmol/L | eGFR
tests.collectionNotes: Do not refrigerate whole blood prior to transport (causes pseudohyperkalaemia). Fill K-EDTA (red top) tube LAST to prevent potassium/calcium contamination.

tests.name: Liver Function Tests Profile (LFTs)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: Bilirubin: <22 µmol/L | ALP: 30-130 U/L | AST: 10-45 U/L | ALT: 5-55 U/L | Total Protein: 60-80 g/L | Albumin: 35-50 g/L | Globulin (calc)
tests.addOnStability: Bilirubin: 72 hours (abnormal results reported with comment) | Enzymes/Proteins: 72 hours
tests.telephoneAlert: ALT/AST >750 U/L (Primary Care only) | Neonatal Total Bilirubin >300 µmol/L | Neonatal Conjugated Bilirubin >25 µmol/L
tests.collectionNotes: Note: GGT (code: GGT) and Conjugated Bilirubin (code: DBIL) are ordered separately if required.

tests.name: Bone Profile
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: Adjusted Calcium: 2.20-2.60 mmol/L | Phosphate: 0.70-1.50 mmol/L | ALP: 30-130 U/L | Albumin: 35-50 g/L | Total Protein: 60-80 g/L
tests.paediatricRanges: Adjusted Ca: <1y NOT APPLICABLE (use Total Ca <=28d 2.00-2.70; 29d-15y 2.20-2.70 mmol/L); 1-15y 2.20-2.70 mmol/L | Phosphate: <=28d 1.30-2.60; 29d-<1y 1.30-2.40; 1-15y 0.80-1.80 mmol/L
tests.addOnStability: Phosphate: 24 hours ONLY (cannot add on after 24h)
tests.telephoneAlert: Corrected Calcium <1.90 or >3.00 mmol/L | Phosphate <0.30 mmol/L
tests.collectionNotes: Take with minimal venous stasis. Adjusted calcium is not valid in infants <1 year.

tests.name: Thyroid Function Tests (TSH & Free T4)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.mri: No repeat TSH or FT4 analysis within 28 days
tests.collectionNotes: State if patient is pregnant (trimester) or taking levothyroxine/carbimazole/amiodarone.

tests.name: Lipid Profile (Cholesterol, Triglycerides, HDL, LDL)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: Total cholesterol, Triglycerides, HDL, calculated LDL (Friedewald equation; only valid if TGs <4.5 mmol/L), Cholesterol:HDL ratio.
tests.collectionNotes: Non-fasting acceptable for routine cardiovascular risk screening; fasting required if triglycerides significantly elevated.

tests.name: Iron Studies (Iron, TIBC, Transferrin Saturation) & Ferritin
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: Iron: 9.0-34.5 µmol/L | TIBC: 45-80 µmol/L | Transferrin Sat: M 20-50%, F 20-45% | Ferritin: M 30-400 µg/L, F <40y 13-150, F 40-60y 13-250, F >60y 30-400 µg/L
tests.collectionNotes: Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant and may be elevated in inflammation/infection.

tests.name: Troponin T (High-Sensitivity TnT)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: 0-13 ng/L (Refer to NHS A&A acute chest pain pathway)
tests.collectionNotes: Note: NT-proBNP is NOT provided by Biochemistry—contact Cardiology Day Unit (01563 827947 / cardiologydayunit@aapct.scot.nhs.uk).

tests.name: CRP, Amylase, Creatine Kinase (CK), LDH, Magnesium & Urate
tests.trakCode: CRP / AM / CK / LDHI / MG / URA
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: CRP: <10 mg/L | Amylase: 0-100 U/L | CK: M 40-320, F 25-200 U/L | LDH: 0-250 U/L | Mg: 0.70-1.00 mmol/L | Urate: M 200-430, F 140-360 µmol/L
tests.telephoneAlert: CRP >300 mg/L (Primary Care only) | Amylase >200 U/L | CK >5000 U/L | Mg <0.40 or >2.00 mmol/L
tests.collectionNotes: CRITICAL FOR RASBURICASE: Urate samples taken while patients are receiving rasburicase must reach the laboratory within 30 minutes (ideally on ice) and be interpreted with caution.

tests.name: Bicarbonate & Plasma / Urine Osmolality
tests.location: In-House (BIC: XH & Ayr | OSM & UOSM: XH Only)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (Blood) | White 20 mL Universal (Urine Osmolality)
tests.tat: BIC & Plasma OSM: 1 day | Urine OSM: 2 days
tests.referenceRange: Bicarbonate: <16y 19-28, >=16y 22-29 mmol/L | Plasma Osmolality: 275-295 mosm/kg | Urine Osmolality: Interpret in clinical context
tests.collectionNotes: Plasma osmolality may be processed urgently on consultant request—telephone Crosshouse lab (01563 827408) to discuss. Note: Blood gases & blood ketones are POCT only (not performed in main lab).

tests.name: Glucose (Plasma & CSF) & Lactate
tests.location: In-House (GLU & LACT: XH & Ayr | CSF Glucose: XH Only)
tests.tubeType: Yellow Top (2.7 mL Potassium Fluoride / EDTA)
tests.referenceRange: Fasting Plasma Glucose: 3.5-6.0 mmol/L | CSF Glucose: >70% of simultaneous plasma glucose | Lactate: 0.7-2.0 mmol/L
tests.telephoneAlert: Glucose <2.5 or >30.0 mmol/L (>=15 mmol/L if <16y) | Lactate >4.0 mmol/L
tests.collectionNotes: MUST use Yellow-top Potassium Fluoride tube for all glucose and lactate requests (including CSF and fluids). Take simultaneous blood glucose when sampling CSF.

tests.name: Haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)
tests.tubeType: Red Top (2.7 mL Potassium EDTA — dedicated Biochemistry tube)
tests.referenceRange: 20-41 mmol/mol Hb (IFCC)
tests.collectionNotes: Requires a dedicated Biochemistry Red-top EDTA tube IN ADDITION to any Haematology FBC tube (tubes cannot be shared).

tests.name: Ammonia (Plasma)
tests.tubeType: Red Top (2.7 mL Potassium EDTA — dedicated tube)
tests.referenceRange: <=28 days: 0-100 µmol/L | >28 days: Male 16-60 µmol/L, Female 11-51 µmol/L
tests.addOnStability: Not suitable for add-on (must reach lab within 4h)
tests.collectionNotes: TIME-CRITICAL: Sample MUST reach the laboratory within 4 hours of collection. Free-flowing venepuncture without prolonged tourniquet stasis; dedicated Red-top EDTA tube.

tests.name: Vitamin B12 & Folate
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.tat: 1 day (Note: Folate takes up to 80 mins — do NOT mark routine folate urgent)
tests.referenceRange: Vitamin B12: 197-771 ng/L | Folate: 3.9-26.8 µg/L
tests.collectionNotes: Do NOT request Folate on urgent forms unless genuinely acute—folate analysis takes up to 80 minutes and delays authorisation of urgent U&Es/LFTs on the same sample.

tests.name: Vitamin D (25-OH Cholecalciferol)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.referenceRange: Reported with interpretative guidance on report.
tests.mri: RESTRICTED: Not routinely available for Primary Care (eff. 02/11/26). No repeat testing within 340 days for patients >= 18 years.
tests.collectionNotes: Subject to strict Minimum Re-testing Interval (340 days in adults >=18y) and Primary Care restriction. Contact Duty Biochemist (01563 827477) for clinical exceptions.

tests.name: Cortisol, Synacthen Test, Prolactin, LH, FSH, Oestradiol, Progesterone & Testosterone
tests.trakCode: CORT / PROL / LH / FSH / OEST / PROG / TEST
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin) [Note: Short Synacthen requires Red + 3x timed Orange tubes]
tests.tat: 1 day (Macroprolactin screen if Prolactin >700 mU/L: 7 days)
tests.referenceRange: Cortisol: 6-10am 133-537, 4-8pm 68-327 nmol/L; Post-Synacthen >450 nmol/L; Post-Dexamethasone <50 nmol/L | Prolactin: M 0-350, F 0-500 mU/L | Progesterone: Day 21 >20 nmol/L = ovulation | Testosterone: M 8.6-29.0 (fasting 8-10am), F <1.7 nmol/L
tests.telephoneAlert: Cortisol <50 nmol/L (unless part of Dexamethasone suppression test)
tests.collectionNotes: Random cortisol is rarely diagnostic. Male testosterone has diurnal variation—collect fasting between 08:00-10:00. For Short Synacthen Test kit, contact Pharmacy ext. 27153/27154.

tests.name: Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)
tests.tubeType: Red Top (2.7 mL Potassium EDTA — dedicated Biochemistry tube)
tests.referenceRange: 1.6-6.9 pmol/L (Interpret alongside simultaneous adjusted calcium)
tests.collectionNotes: MUST use dedicated Red-top EDTA tube (in addition to any FBC tube) and send alongside an Orange-top tube for Bone Profile.

tests.name: Tumour Markers (AFP, CA 125, CA 19-9, CEA, PSA) & Serum HCG
tests.trakCode: AFP / C125 / C199 / CEA / PSA / HCG
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin)
tests.tat: 1 day (Urgent HCG from Ayr: phone Ayr lab x14258 for taxi transfer to XH)
tests.referenceRange: AFP: <6 kU/L | CA 125: <35 kU/L | CA 19-9: <34 kU/L | CEA: <5.0 µg/L | PSA: <=69y 0-2.9, 70-79y 0-4.9 µg/L (>=80y refer to Scottish Referral Guidelines) | HCG: <5 U/L (tumour marker range)
tests.collectionNotes: If an urgent serum HCG is required at University Hospital Ayr (e.g., suspected ectopic pregnancy), phone Ayr Biochemistry (x14258) so the sample is dispatched immediately by taxi to Crosshouse.

tests.name: Serum Protein Electrophoresis, Immunoglobulins, Bence Jones Protein & Cryoglobulin
tests.location: In-House (IG: XH & Ayr | SPEP, BJP, Cryoglobulin: XH Only)
tests.tubeType: White Top 7.5 mL Serum (SPEP & 2x White for Cryoglobulin) | Orange Top (IG) | White 20 mL Universal Urine (BJP)
tests.tat: IG: 1 day | SPEP & BJP & Cryoglobulin: Up to 7 days
tests.referenceRange: IgG: 6.0-16.0 g/L | IgA: 0.8-4.0 g/L | IgM: 0.5-2.0 g/L | BJP: Normally negative (early morning urine preferred) | Cryoglobulin: Normally absent
tests.paediatricRanges: Age-specific IgA, IgG, IgM ranges in Appendix 2 (e.g. IgG <=14d 5.0-17.0; 4-6m 2.4-8.8; 4-6y 4.9-16.1 g/L)
tests.mri: Protein Electrophoresis: No repeat within 21 days | Bence Jones Protein: No repeat within 120 days
tests.collectionNotes: SPEP requires a White-top (clotted serum) tube. CRYOGLOBULIN: Must pre-arrange with Crosshouse lab (x27408) for a warm flask; patient must attend and sample must arrive BEFORE 13:00.

tests.name: In-House Drug Monitoring & Toxicology (Paracetamol, Salicylate, Ethanol, Lithium, Digoxin, Anticonvulsants, Vancomycin, Gentamicin, Tobramycin, Theophylline)
tests.trakCode: PARA / SAL / ETH / LI / DIG / CARB / PHEN / PHEB / VALP / THEO / GENT / TOBR / VANC
tests.location: In-House (PARA, SAL, ETH, GENT, VANC: XH & Ayr | LI, DIG, CARB, PHEN, PHEB, VALP, THEO, TOBR: XH Only)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (5.5 mL Lithium Heparin) [EXCEPTION: Lithium requires White Top 7.5 mL Serum]
tests.referenceRange: Lithium: 0.4-1.0 mmol/L (12h post-dose) | Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 µg/L (>=6h post-dose) | Carbamazepine: 4-12 mg/L (pre-dose) | Phenytoin: 10-20 mg/L | Phenobarbitone: 15-40 mg/L | Valproate: 50-100 mg/L | Theophylline: 10-20 mg/L (pre-dose or 8h post slow-release)
tests.telephoneAlert: Lithium >1.50 mmol/L | Digoxin >2.5 µg/L | Phenytoin >25 mg/L | Phenobarbitone >70 mg/L | Carbamazepine >25 mg/L | Theophylline >25 mg/L | Salicylate >300 mg/L | Paracetamol >7 mg/L | Ethanol: Any detectable level in paediatrics
tests.collectionNotes: State exact time of last dose and sample collection. Lithium MUST be collected in a White-top plain serum tube 12 hours post-dose. Gentamicin/Tobramycin/Vancomycin: refer to NHS A&A Pharmacy dosing protocols.

tests.name: CSF Protein, CSF Glucose & CSF Xanthochromia (Spectrophotometry)
tests.location: In-House (CPRO & CGLU: XH Only) | Xanthochromia: Temporarily Referred to QEUH Glasgow
tests.referralLab: Biochemistry, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital (QEUH), Glasgow (temporary referral for Xanthochromia)
tests.tubeType: CSF Protein & Xanthochromia: White Universal (min 1.0 mL, last/least blood-stained fraction) | CSF Glucose: Yellow Top (Fluoride)
tests.referenceRange: CSF Protein: 0.15-0.45 g/L | CSF Glucose: >70% of simultaneous plasma glucose | Xanthochromia: Investigates CT-negative SAH (>=12h post-onset)
tests.collectionNotes: XANTHOCHROMIA: Sample >=12 hours after headache onset. Protect from light immediately (place in brown envelope), DO NOT use pneumatic tube, hand-deliver so it is centrifuged within 15 minutes (taxi from Ayr). Take concurrent blood for bilirubin, total protein & glucose. Alert lab by phone if TB meningitis suspected.

tests.name: Body Fluid Biochemistry (Ascitic, Pleural, Drain, Synovial, Dialysate, Vitreous)
tests.trakCode: Fluid Biochemistry (Specify exact fluid type on request)
tests.tubeType: White Top 7.5 mL Plain Tube (or 20 mL White Universal) | Yellow Top 2.7 mL Fluoride for Glucose & Lactate
tests.sampleType: Ascitic, pleural, drain, synovial, dialysate, or vitreous fluid
tests.referenceRange: No reference ranges available for fluid analysis (interpret using Light's criteria / SAAG). Available: Albumin, Amylase, Bicarbonate, Bilirubin, Calcium, Cholesterol, Creatinine, Glucose, HDL, Lactate, LDH, Na, Phosphate, Protein, Triglyceride, Urate, Urea.
tests.collectionNotes: Note: Cell count/microscopy goes to Microbiology; crystal microscopy goes to Cellular Pathology (send separate containers and forms to each lab). Use Yellow-top fluoride tube for fluid glucose/lactate (except dialysate).

tests.name: Urine Biochemistry (ACR, PCR, Electrolytes, Calcium, 24hr Collections, Metadrenalines & Catecholamines)
tests.trakCode: MALB / UPCR / URE / UREL / UCA / CA24 / CACR / CRCL / METP / CATP / AHIA / CHIA
tests.tubeType: White 20 mL Universal (Spot) OR 24-Hour Urine Collection Container (Acidified for 5-HIAA/Oxalate)
tests.sampleType: Spot Urine or 24-Hour Urine (plus Orange blood tube during collection for Creatinine Clearance)
tests.referenceRange: ACR: M <2.5, F <3.5 mg/mmol | PCR: 0-0.014 g/mmol | 24h Protein: 0.01-0.11 g/24h | 24h Calcium: 2.5-7.5 mmol/24h | Ca:Creat ratio: 0.04-0.70 mmol/mol | Creat Clearance: 80-120 mL/min | 5-HIAA: 0-50 µmol/24h | Metadrenalines (>=18y): Normet <650, Met <350, 3-MT <550 nmol/24h
tests.paediatricRanges: Age-adjusted Ca:Creat ratio, 5-HIAA, and Catecholamine metabolites (<18y: CATP) listed in Appendix 2
tests.collectionNotes: For Creatinine Clearance (CRCL), ensure blood sample is taken during the 24h urine collection period. For children <18y investigating neuroblastoma, request Catecholamine metabolites (CATP) on spot urine rather than 24h Metadrenalines.

tests.name: Faecal Tests: qFIT (Occult Blood), Faecal Calprotectin & Faecal Elastase
tests.trakCode: qFIT (N/O - Picker) | Calprotectin: CALP (Referred) | Elastase: ELAS (Referred)
tests.location: qFIT: In-House (XH Only) | Calprotectin: GRI | Elastase: Western General Edinburgh
tests.referralLab: Glasgow Royal Infirmary (Calprotectin) / Edinburgh Western General (Elastase)
tests.tubeType: qFIT: Alpha qFIT 'Picker' | Calprotectin & Elastase: Blue-capped Faeces Container (send 2 separate pots if both requested)
tests.tat: qFIT: 7 days | Calprotectin: 28 days | Elastase: 31 days
tests.referenceRange: qFIT: 0-10 µg Hb/g faeces | Calprotectin & Elastase: Reported by referral laboratory
tests.mri: Faecal Calprotectin: No repeat testing within 120 days
tests.collectionNotes: qFIT return envelope MUST contain a labelled picker AND completed Biochemistry request form. If requesting BOTH Calprotectin (GRI) and Elastase (Edinburgh), send TWO separate blue faeces pots (may be from the same bowel movement).

tests.name: Alpha-1-Antitrypsin (Level & Phenotyping), Caeruloplasmin, Copper & ACE
tests.location: AAT Level: In-House (XH) | Phenotyping, Caeruloplasmin, Copper, ACE: Referred
tests.referralLab: Edinburgh Western General (AAT Phenotype) / GRI (Caeruloplasmin, Copper) / Hairmyres (Serum ACE) / Charing Cross (CSF ACE)
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (AAT, Plasma Copper) | White Top (Caeruloplasmin, Serum ACE) | White Universal 25 mL (24h/Urine Copper)
tests.tat: AAT level: 1 day | Caeruloplasmin: 7 days | AAT Phenotype: 14 days | Serum ACE: 21 days | Copper: 28 days
tests.referenceRange: Alpha-1-antitrypsin: 1.1-2.1 g/L | Referral ranges on report
tests.collectionNotes: Note: CSF ACE (min 0.5 mL in white universal) goes to Charing Cross Hospital (TAT 56 days); Serum ACE goes to Hairmyres.

tests.name: Trace Elements & Fat/Water-Soluble Vitamins (Zinc, Selenium, Lead, Mercury, Chromium, Cobalt, Vit A/B1/B2/B6/C/E/K)
tests.trakCode: ZINC / SEL / LEAD / MERC / CR / CO / ALU / MANG / VITA / VB1 / VB2 / VB6 / VITC / VITE / VITK
tests.referralLab: Scottish Trace Element and Micronutrient Diagnostic and Research Laboratory (STEMDRL), Glasgow
tests.tubeType: Orange Top (Selenium requires own dedicated tube; Vit A/B2/B6/E/K PROTECT FROM LIGHT) | Red Top (Chromium, Cobalt, Mercury; Lead accepts Red or Orange)
tests.referenceRange: Reported by STEMDRL Glasgow.
tests.paediatricRanges: Lead: Paediatric containers are UNSUITABLE (min volume 350 µL in standard Red/Orange tube).
tests.addOnStability: Vitamin C: Must arrive within 4 hours of collection
tests.collectionNotes: CRITICAL PRE-ANALYTICAL RULES: 1) Protect Vitamins A, B2, B6, E, K from light (wrap in foil/brown bag). 2) Vitamin C must arrive at lab within 4 hours. 3) Selenium requires its own unshared Orange tube. 4) Lead cannot use paediatric tubes.

tests.name: Immunosuppressants, Biologic Levels & TPMT (Tacrolimus, Ciclosporin, Sirolimus, Mycophenolate, Infliximab, Adalimumab, TPMT, 6-TGN)
tests.trakCode: TACR / CYCL / SIRO / MPAA / IFMB / ADAL / TPMT / TGN
tests.referralLab: QEUH Glasgow (Tacrolimus, Ciclosporin, Sirolimus, Infliximab, Adalimumab) / South Manchester (Mycophenolate) / Sandwell (TPMT) / Birmingham (6-TGN)
tests.tubeType: Red Top 2.7 mL EDTA (Tacrolimus, Ciclosporin, Sirolimus, Mycophenolate, TPMT, 6-TGN) | White Top Serum (Infliximab, Adalimumab)
tests.tat: Tacrolimus/Ciclosporin/Sirolimus: 7 days | Infliximab/Adalimumab/6-TGN: 14 days | Mycophenolate: 21 days | TPMT: 28 days
tests.referenceRange: Reported by performing laboratory.
tests.collectionNotes: Take tacrolimus/ciclosporin/sirolimus immediately pre-dose (trough) and state exact dose timing on form.

tests.name: Neuroimmunology, Oligoclonal Bands, Tau (Beta-2 Transferrin), Tryptase & Renal/Endocrine Antibodies
tests.trakCode: OLIG / CTAU / ACRA / A4AM / VGKC / NMDA / TRYP / PLA2 / TPO / TRAB / ICAP
tests.referralLab: QEUH Immunology & Neuroimmunology Glasgow / Sheffield PRU (Tau) / GRI (TPO, TRAb) / Ninewells (PLA2R)
tests.tubeType: White Top 7.5 mL Serum (Paired White Serum + White Universal CSF required for Oligoclonal Bands)
tests.tat: TPO/TRAb: 7 days | NMDA/Islet/Ovarian: 14 days | Oligoclonal bands/MOG/Aquaporin/LGI1/Tryptase: 16 days | PLA2R: 21 days | Tau/VGCC: 28-30 days
tests.referenceRange: Reported by referral laboratory.
tests.collectionNotes: Oligoclonal bands (OLIG) MUST have paired CSF and serum taken concurrently. Beta-2 transferrin (CTAU) investigates CSF rhinorrhoea/otorrhoea. Mast cell tryptase (TRYP): take acute sample within 1-3h of anaphylaxis + baseline >=24h.

tests.name: Time-Critical Referred Tests: ACTH, Renin, Plasma Metadrenalines, Homocysteine, Insulin, C-Peptide, Chromogranin A, Proinsulin & CSF Neurotransmitters
tests.trakCode: ACTH / REN / PFMS / HCYS / INSU / CPEP / CHGR / PROI / Gut Hormones (N/O) / CSF Neurotransmitters (N/O)
tests.referralLab: GRI Biochemistry / Edinburgh Western General / Sheffield PRU / UCLH London / Guildford RSCH
tests.tubeType: Red Top EDTA (ACTH, Renin, Plasma Metadrenalines, Homocysteine, Methylmalonic acid) | Orange Top (Insulin, C-Peptide) | White Top (Proinsulin)
tests.referenceRange: Reported by referral laboratory.
tests.collectionNotes: STRICT ARRIVAL TIMES AT LAB: Proinsulin <=30 mins | Homocysteine & Plasma Metadrenalines <=2 hours | Chromogranin A <=3 hours | ACTH, Renin, C-Peptide, Insulin, Methylmalonic acid <=4 hours. Gut hormones require 2x Orange+Trasylol tubes from lab. CSF Neurotransmitters MUST be pre-arranged with Duty Biochemist (dry ice).

tests.name: Porphyria Screen (Blood/Urine PBG), Haemochromatosis (HFE), Gilbert's, PKU & Renal Stone Analysis
tests.trakCode: BPOR / UPOR / PBG (N/O) / HGNE / GILB / STON
tests.referralLab: QEUH Glasgow (Porphyria, HFE, PKU) / Ninewells (Gilbert's) / UCLH London (Renal Stone)
tests.tubeType: Porphyria: Red Blood + White Universal Urine (PROTECT ALL FROM LIGHT) | HFE & Gilbert's: 2x Red Top | Stone: Dry White Universal
tests.tat: PBG/PKU: 7 days | Porphyrins: 16 days | Gilbert's/Stone: 28 days | HFE gene: 40 days
tests.referenceRange: Reported by referral laboratory.
tests.collectionNotes: ALL porphyrin and PBG samples MUST be protected from light immediately after collection.
